keys.default: Your account has been marked inactive. If you would like to reactivate your account, please contact your administrator.
keys.description: Message shown at login to a user whose account status is `Inactive`. Each key of `app:locked_account_statuses` defines an account status that blocks login, with its message.

keys.default: Your account has been locked for security reasons. Please contact your administrator.
keys.description: Message shown at login to a user whose account status is `Locked`. Each key of `app:locked_account_statuses` defines an account status that blocks login, with its message.
Path to the bundled PMTiles file on disk

Maximum size of a JSON request body accepted by the API, the TAXII server and the other HTTP routes, such as `50mb`. Raise it if large requests are rejected. Unset, `50mb`, and from 7.261119 `10mb` with `app:http:secure_by_default`. From 7.261119, the TAXII API root advertises this limit, in bytes, as its `max_content_length` (before, a fixed 100 MB).
Identifier of this node in a cluster, used to register the node and to synchronize caches; a random UUID is generated at each start when empty. Set it to keep the same identity across restarts.
Logs every API call, with its duration, size and memory usage, at info level. Use it to analyze performance; it produces a lot of logs.

How the platform runs its Python scripts (indicator syntax check, STIX pattern generation): `native` runs them in an interpreter embedded in the platform process; any other value starts a `python3` child process for each call.

Maximum number of elements grouped into one batched load when an API request resolves related data (creators, markings, relations...). Lower it if batched queries to the search engine get too large.

Disable Search Engine compatibility matrix verification. __Caution__: OpenCTI was developed in compliance with the compatibility matrix. Setting the parameter to `false` may result in negative impacts. Until 7.261030 only: from 7.261109 the platform ignores it and logs a warning.

`elk` or `opensearch`, default is `auto`, please put `elk` if you use token auth. Until 7.261030 only: from 7.261109 the platform ignores it, logs a warning, and reads `elasticsearch:engine_client` instead.

Suffix appended to the alias name when the platform creates an index (for example `opencti_stix_domain_objects-000001`). Rollover then increments it. Changing it only affects indices created afterwards.
Prefix for the indices

Internal: helper for reindex migrations (`off`, `standard` or `old`). On a new platform any value other than `off` creates the templates and indices with that mapping, then stops the process; on an existing platform it fails at start. Do not change it.

Maximum number of operations sent in one bulk request to the search engine during mass updates (relation and denormalization updates, migrations). Lower it if bulk requests time out or exceed the cluster's request size.

Number of bulk requests or fetch batches the platform sends to the search engine in parallel during mass updates and migrations. Raise it on a large cluster to speed them up, lower it to reduce the load.
Maximum number of objects gathered from the containers of an entity when building its containers graph; once reached, the platform stops reading more containers.
Maximum number of containers (or contained elements) loaded to resolve related containers and the containers graph of an entity. Raise it to see more containers at the cost of heavier queries.
Number of documents after which an index rolls over, written into the lifecycle policy the platform creates with its indices (ILM `max_docs` on Elasticsearch, ISM `min_doc_count` on OpenSearch).
Maximum number of results one search page can return; a larger requested page size is capped to this value. Also the batch size of internal loops that load elements by id.

Primary shard size after which an index rolls over (for example `50gb`), written into the lifecycle policy the platform creates with its indices (ILM `max_primary_shard_size` on Elasticsearch, ISM `min_primary_shard_size` on OpenSearch).
Index setting `max_result_window` (maximum offset plus size of a search), set in the platform's core settings template at each start and applied to indices created afterwards.
Number of times the search engine client retries a failed request before returning an error.

Maximum number of entities (identities, countries, kill chain phases) loaded to sort lists by a computed column such as author or country. Raise it if sorting by these columns shows `Unknown` on a large dataset.
Number of replicas of each index, set in the platform's core settings template at each start and applied to indices created afterwards. Unset, the search engine default applies.
Number of primary shards of each index, set in the platform's core settings template at each start and applied to indices created afterwards. Unset, the search engine default applies.
